approach: Add a FromOpenProject(donor) classmethod to flexicon.FLExProject that builds a view over a cache the host already opened: validate the donor, allocate with cls.__new__(cls), borrow project/lp/lexDB/writeEnabled, force _undoable=False, and mark the instance with _attached_donor. Guard CloseProject (no-op), SaveChanges and the disposing paths (FP_RuntimeError naming FromOpenProject), and make the UndoableOperation refusal attached-view aware. All source lands in the flexicon repo; FlexToolsMCP only runs the cross-repo regression gate.

decisions.decision: Construct the attached view with cls.__new__(cls) and assign exactly project, lp, lexDB, writeEnabled
decisions.why: flexicon.FLExProject has no __init__ (all state is born in OpenProject) and every facade property lazily builds its operations object from self, so five assignments give a complete facade over a borrowed cache
decisions.rejected: Adding a shared __init__ for both OpenProject and the bridge, which would break the documented no-argument FLExProject() construction; and copying the donor __dict__ wholesale, which drags flexlibs-private state onto a flexicon instance

decisions.decision: Force _undoable=False on the view AND rewrite the UndoableOperation refusal message for attached views
decisions.why: flexlibs opens a session-long BeginNonUndoableTask envelope when write-enabled (flexlibs/code/FLExProject.py:262), so Phase 1 Transaction is the only correct mode; but undoable now defaults to True since flexicon 4.4.0, so the existing refusal text blames an OpenProject argument nobody passed
decisions.rejected: Honouring the donors mode (flexlibs has no _undoable at all), and leaving the existing message unchanged (an inaccurate error in the first path a migrating module hits)

decisions.decision: Check _attached_donor BEFORE the existing issue-243 depth guard in SaveChanges
decisions.why: A write-enabled flexlibs donor holds CurrentDepth at 1 all session, so SaveChanges already fails today but with a transaction-depth message that says nothing about the donor; a read-only donor would instead hit FP_ReadOnlyError. Both are the wrong story.
decisions.rejected: Relying on the existing depth guard alone

decisions.decision: Idempotence returns the donor object itself (identity), not a copy or wrapper
decisions.why: Under the MCP the donor is already a flexicon FLExProject that owns its project; returning it unchanged preserves that ownership, its Phase 2 mode, and its cached operations objects
decisions.rejected: Always building a fresh view, which would silently downgrade an MCP session to Phase 1 and leave two objects believing they own one cache

decisions.decision: Validate the donor at the seam and raise FP_ParameterError naming every missing attribute plus type(donor).__module__
decisions.why: Replaces an AttributeError fifty frames deep inside an operation; __module__ is the only honest discriminator because both classes are named FLExProject
decisions.rejected: hasattr duck typing with no error (the current silent-failure behaviour) and inventing a new exception type

decisions.decision: CP2 unit tests use a fake donor with no requires_live_project marker; CP3 live verification gates CP1 from shipping
decisions.why: The bridge opens nothing, so the only registered pytest marker would be a lie; but a fake cannot observe T3.2 (whether a Phase 1 write inside the host envelope reaches disk), and shipping a seam whose writes may silently not persist repeats the original incident
decisions.rejected: Shipping on unit tests alone and letting field use decide

decisions.decision: The attached-view SaveChanges refusal must not repeat the existing "use CloseProject() instead" advice
decisions.why: R3 makes CloseProject() a silent no-op on a view, so the standing advice attached to the issue-243 depth guard would produce a run that reports success and writes nothing -- the exact green-run-that-is-not-green failure this feature exists to end
decisions.rejected: Inheriting the existing wording, and making CloseProject() raise on a view (SPEC 3b forbids it)

decisions.decision: Keep the read-only check AHEAD of the attached-view branch in UndoableOperation.__enter__, rejecting QC P0 as stated; pin the behaviour with a named test instead
decisions.why: Contract section 4 "never branch on writeEnabled" is Invariant A about how a guard DETECTS a view, not an ordering rule. A read-only view cannot write by any route, so FP_ReadOnlyError is true and actionable; the attached-view message points at Transaction(), which also fails read-only - a wrong answer shaped like a helpful one. SaveChanges is the opposite case (a write-enabled view must still refuse) which is why the orders differ.
decisions.rejected: Reordering to put the attached-view check first, which would emit misleading Transaction() advice to a caller who cannot write at all

decisions.decision: Widen the 6000-char source-window assertion in test_transaction_honesty.py to 9000 rather than compressing the SaveChanges docstring to fit it
decisions.why: The docstring had been squeezed to telegraphic stubs with 44 chars of headroom; the repo precedent (documented in that test twice, 1000->2500->6000) is that the window assumption is the thing that is wrong, not the prose. The assertion tests that both methods resolve the same accessor, not a docstring length budget.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the compressed stubs, which would have shipped cryptic docs and left any future docstring edit breaking an unrelated test

decisions.decision: T3.2 gate PASSES - ship CP1 with _undoable=False alone, no MainCacheAccessor flush added to contract section 2.2
decisions.why: A Transaction() write through an attached view, with no module-side save, reached the .fwdata on both a scratch copy and Sena 3, verified by FlexTools own read-back in a fresh process, by grep over the raw file, and by the MCP stack
decisions.rejected: Adding an explicit flush step to contract 2.2 and returning the feature to plan - the branch T016 mandates if the value had not persisted

decisions.decision: T025 also converted Main()'s example body from project.* to fx.*
decisions.why: The task said to add the fx = FromOpenProject(project) line but did not mention the accessor calls; leaving them would define fx and never use it, teaching readers the line is decorative
decisions.rejected: Adding fx and leaving project.LexEntry throughout - literal to the task text but self-contradicting as a template. The CRITICAL REQUIREMENT preamble was left untouched as instructed, and the template has no Shape B examples to preserve.

decisions.decision: Added a stamped _TESTED_AGAINST constant plus an advisory version warning to the flexicon template; narrowed the T4.2c ratchet from no-version-comparison to no-version-comparison-that-gates
decisions.why: User asked for the tested-against version to be tracked so the module warns when running on something older. Contract 8.2 bans a version FLOOR (one that gates), not an advisory note; a wrong advisory costs a spurious warning, never a working module. Stamping at generation time avoids the hand-maintained rot already found in the REQUIRES: Flexicon version 2.0+ line.
decisions.rejected: A hard minimum version - would refuse a working editable install today, since its metadata reads 4.1.1 while the source is 4.6.0. Also rejected: recording the version without comparing, which leaves silent drift undetected.

plan.summary: Resumed and finished the plan step: verified every line reference in plan.md/research.md/data-model.md/contracts against the live flexicon and flexlibs trees, fixed the case-broken ./SPEC.md link left by the lowercase rename, and added R7 after finding that the SaveChanges guards standing advice is a trap on an attached view.
plan.key_finding: The existing SaveChanges docstring tells callers to use CloseProject() instead when CurrentDepth > 0 -- but R3 makes CloseProject() a silent no-op on an attached view, so following that advice yields a green run that writes nothing. The attached-view refusal must replace the advice, not just the diagnosis; T2.2b now asserts the message does NOT contain CloseProject.
